previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman was admitted after a mechanical fall at home, during which she struck her head but denied loss of consciousness. She had a scalp laceration repaired with staples, and imaging showed no acute intracranial or cervical spine injury. Admission labs revealed elevated creatinine and hypokalemia, prompting adjustment of her metolazone dose from three to two times per week. A chest X-ray showed atelectasis without signs of infection, and asymptomatic pyuria was noted but not treated. She remained stable, with no cardiac or neurologic complications, and was discharged home with follow-up in the heart failure clinic and instructions for staple removal and BMP monitoring.
problems: Laceration without foreign body of scalp, initial encounter
Other fall on same level, initial encounter
Hypertensive heart disease with heart failure

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  MRCP

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with CAD, CHF, cystic neoplasm of pancreas with
enlarging pancreatic mass.  // Evaluate pancreatic mass for malignant
characteristics, gastric outlet obstruction.

TECHNIQUE:  T1- and T2-weighted multiplanar images of the abdomen were
acquired in a 1.5 T magnet utilizing non-breath hold technique.
Intravenous contrast: 7 mL Gadavist.
Oral contrast:  1 cc of Gadavist mixed with 50 cc of water was administered
for oral contrast.

COMPARISON:  Compared to prior CT dated ___ and MRI dated ___.

FINDINGS: 

Lower Thorax: Within limitations of MRI, there is bilateral atelectasis at the
lung bases.  No pleural or pericardial effusions.  Mild cardiomegaly.  There
is a small fat containing right Bochdalek hernia.

Liver: Liver demonstrates normal contours without morphological signs of liver
cirrhosis.  No hepatic steatosis.  Multiple subcentimeter T2 hyperintense
lesions, compatible with cysts/biliary hamartomas.  No worrisome enhancing
hepatic mass lesions.

Biliary: Gallbladder is present containing small amount of biliary sludge.  No
gallbladder wall thickening or pericholecystic fluid.  No intrahepatic or
extrahepatic biliary duct dilatation.  There is slight mass effect on the
distal common bile duct by the large cystic pancreatic mass, however no
proximal dilatation.  No common bile duct filling defects or
choledocholithiasis.

Pancreas: There is diffuse pancreatic fatty infiltration.  There has been
interval increase in size of the previously described cystic lesion at the
uncinate process of the pancreas, currently measuring 6.7 x 6.3 x 5.9 cm.  It
measured 1.9 x 1.8 cm on most recent CT dated ___.  The cystic
lesion appears homogeneously hyperintense on the T2 weighted images and
hypointense on the T1 weighted images.  There appears to be a focal area of
irregular wall thickening and/or septation at the inferior aspect of the cyst
(series 2, image 22 and series 8, image 31 and 35) that is more apparent on
today's study.  On the postcontrast images there is no abnormal enhancing soft
tissue nodularity, but assessment of the inferior aspect of the cyst is
limited due to non-breath hold technique.  The mass does cause slight mass
effect on the pancreatic duct, however no proximal dilatation.

There are multiple other T2 hyperintense cystic lesions within the pancreatic
body and tail (series 10, image 20 and 23) measuring up to 5 mm, compatible
with side-branch IPMNs.

The main pancreatic duct measures 3 mm in maximal diameter.  There is no
peripancreatic inflammatory changes or fluid collections.

Spleen: Spleen is normal in size and signal characteristics.  It enhances
homogeneously without focal mass lesion.

Adrenal Glands: Adrenal glands are normal bilaterally without focal nodules.

Kidneys: There is diffuse atrophy of the right kidney containing multiple
simple and hemorrhagic subcentimeter renal cysts.  The left kidney is normal
in size with good corticomedullary differentiation and adequate excretion
contrast on the more delayed phases.  There are multiple simple renal cortical
cysts.  In addition there is an 8 mm T2 hypointense lesion at the inferior
aspect of the left kidney that appears hyperintense on the T1 weighted images,
stable from prior, most likely hemorrhagic/proteinaceous cyst.  No suspicious
solid masses or hydronephrosis.  No perinephric abnormality.

Gastrointestinal Tract:  There is a small hiatal hernia.  Remainder of the
stomach, visualized small bowel and colon in the upper abdomen are normal in
caliber.  No ascites.No evidence of gastric outlet obstruction on this exam.

Lymph Nodes: No suspicious mesenteric, retroperitoneal or porta hepatis
lymphadenopathy by size criteria.

Vasculature: Chronic aortic dissection is partially visualized.  The diameter
of the abdominal aorta at the hiatus measures 3.5 x 3.1 cm, which has
increased in size when compared to prior MRI dated ___, with
increasing thrombosis within the false lumen.  The celiac, SMA and ___ are
patent arising from the true lumen.

Osseous and Soft Tissue Structures: No suspicious osseous or soft tissue mass
lesions.  Multilevel degenerative disc disease of the lumbar spine.

IMPRESSION: 

1.  Significant interval increase in size of a known cystic pancreatic lesion
in the uncinate process currently measuring 6.7 x 6.3 cm with new focal area
of irregular wall thickening and/or septation at the inferior aspect of the
cyst.  While no abnormal enhancement is noted within the cyst, the exam is
limited by non-breath hold technique.  Findings are concerning for a cystic
pancreatic neoplasm with possible malignant transformation.  Further
evaluation with endoscopic ultrasound and aspiration is recommended.  There is
slight mass effect on the distal common bile duct and the main pancreatic duct
at the pancreatic head by this large cystic lesion, however no proximal
dilatation or evidence of gastric outlet obstruction.

2.  Multiple subcentimeter T2 hyperintense cystic lesions within the
pancreatic body and tail, most likely  side branch IPMNs.

3.  Chronic aortic dissection with interval increase in size of the diameter
of the abdominal aorta measuring up to 3.5 cm with increasing thrombosis
within the false lumen.

RECOMMENDATION(S):  EUS and sampling of the pancreatic cystic mass.

NOTIFICATION:  The findings were discussed with ___, M.D. by ___
___, M.D. on the telephone on ___ at 9:50 AM, 25 minutes after
discovery of the findings.
